title: Seat an aluminium housing on a fixture's datum stops, then lock both toggle clamps
instruction: Set the casting hard into the fixture's corner stops, then close both hold-down clamps over it.
context: Setting a part on a fixture's stops and clamping it is a task of three O*NET occupations: machinists (51-4041.00, 288,300 US jobs in 2025) "align and secure holding fixtures, cutting tools, attachments, accessories, or materials onto machines"; CNC tool operators (51-9161.00, 170,000) "mount, install, align, and secure tools, attachments, fixtures, and workpieces on machines"; welders, cutters, solderers and brazers (51-4121.06, 437,700) "position items in fixtures, jigs, or vises": 896,000 jobs. Here: an aluminium housing in a machining fixture. The hard parts, in order: (1) carry it over the clamp bases, set it down; (2) seat it square against both stops, within 1.0 mm at both ends of each, not turning it; (3) clamp only then: each pad presses 20 N, so a part clamped off a stop is held there, unseated; (4) carry each handle round its whole stroke and past dead centre, or it does not lock; (5) the clamps stand on two sides.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is z = 0. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) Fixture plate, fixed, steel: x 200 to 380 mm, y -160 to +160 mm, 12 mm thick. On it, fixed steel datum stops, 12 mm tall: S1 across the far side, x 330 to 345 mm, y -45 to +45 mm; S2 along the right side, x 280 to 320 mm, y -60 to -50 mm. (2) Splash guard, fixed, steel, 8 mm thick, 400 mm wide, 140 mm tall: x 395 to 403 mm, y -200 to +200 mm. (3) Two vertical hold-down toggle clamps with the linkage of a DESTACO 207-U (handle opening 57 degrees, clamp bar opening 99 degrees), fixed bases (steel foot 50 x 34 x 4 mm, post up to 44 mm above the table, side cheeks). Each is a four-bar linkage of three moving parts, blue: the clamp arm on a pivot 54 mm above the table, 12 mm wide and 8 mm thick, with a red 12 x 12 x 8 mm pad under its end; the handle on a second pivot 32 mm behind and 26 mm above the table, 12 x 8 mm, with a black grip 24 mm wide and 14 mm thick over its last 45 mm and a 16 mm crank; a grey connecting link, 32 mm, from the crank to a pin 7 mm from the arm's pivot. C1 on the near side: arm pivot x 236 mm, y -25 mm; arm 62 mm toward +x, pad centre 52 mm from its pivot (x 288 mm); handle 110 mm. C2 on the left side: arm pivot x 300 mm, y +125 mm; arm 99 mm toward -y, pad centre 91 mm out (y +34 mm); handle 145 mm. Both start open on their stops: handle 57 degrees back from vertical, away from the casting; arm 99 degrees up from flat. Pushing the handle forward swings the arm down; its pad lands on the casting's top (42 mm above the table) about 3 degrees before the handle is vertical. Vertical is the linkage's dead centre: the pad presses 25 N (C1) or 29 N (C2), a spindle with a rubber cap set for a light press. The handle's stop is 1.5 degrees past vertical: there the pad presses 20 N, and that force, through the link, holds the handle on its stop (over-centre lock); about 2.2 N (C1) or 2.8 N (C2) back at the grip reopens it. Nothing drives a clamp: the handle needs about 0.3 N at its grip (its weight) for most of the stroke, rising to a peak of 2.2 N (C1) or 2.7 N (C2) 15 mm from its end in the last 2 degrees before vertical. Let go short of vertical a clamp does not lock: from about 40 degrees back the arm's weight lowers it onto the casting and the handle stays short of vertical; nearer its open stop it falls back open. With nothing under the pad a handle can go over centre onto its stop: shut on nothing. (4) Staging block, fixed, white HDPE, 100 (x) x 150 (y) x 20 mm: x 170 to 270 mm, y +170 to +320 mm. (5) Casting, loose: an aluminium housing, 60 (x) x 100 (y) x 30 mm tall, made as a 6061 aluminium block of that size pocketed from below to 5 mm walls and a 5 mm top (0.18 kg at 2.70 g/cm3), friction about 0.3, grey, lying right way up on the block, its centre at x 220 mm, y +245 mm, its 100 mm side along y. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the casting's pose, both clamps' joint angles and both grippers; a missing or non-finite reading scores 0. Seated: the casting lies flat on the plate (tilt at most 1 degree, lowest corner within 1.5 mm of the plate's top), its far face within 1.0 mm of S1 (gap or overlap) at both ends of S1's 90 mm face (40 mm either side of its centre) and its right face within 1.0 mm of S2 at both ends of S2's 40 mm face (x 285 and 315 mm); a stop point the face does not cover (3 mm in from its edges) counts as a miss. Shut: a handle over centre, 0.5 degree or more past vertical (its stop is at 1.5). Locked: shut, with the centre of the pad's underside between 1.5 mm into the casting's top face and 0.5 mm above it, and at least 4 mm inside the face's edges (the pad then presses it with 20 N). A clamp shut on nothing is not locked. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the casting and from both clamps, and over that 1 s the casting moves at most 1 mm and turns at most 1 degree and neither handle turns over 2 degrees. Score 0 if not hands off or if not seated (this includes a casting clamped off its stops: its pads hold it there). Otherwise: 1.0 both clamps locked; 0.5 one locked; 0.25 none locked. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial, per condition: seated, a 1.0 mm feeler gauge at each end of each stop and a level on the casting's top; locked (each clamp), the handle against its over-centre stop (past vertical on a square), a 0.5 mm feeler gauge does not slide under the pad, and a 1 N pull back on a spring scale at the grip leaves it shut; for 1.0 also a proof test with both clamps locked: a 20 N pull on a spring scale, straight up and then sideways away from the stops, does not move the casting on a dial indicator; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand, the dial indicator (1 mm) and 30 fps video of the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Open both clamps (handles back on their open stops, arms up), clear the plate and wipe chips off the stops, and lay the casting right way up on the staging block with its centre at x 220 mm, y +245 mm and its 100 mm side along y. Nothing is consumed; check each pad's press (20 N with the handle on its stop, set by the spindle) once a session and change the pads every few hundred closings.
fidelity: Linkage after the DESTACO 207-U (57, 99 degree openings), arm reach of the 207-U and 210-U (pads 52, 91 mm out); link and handle lengths, spindle stiffness and the 20 N press are est. Handle, link and arm are jointed bodies; a declared rule closes the four-bar loop each 20 Hz step (arm and link to their linkage angles, the pad's load passed back to the handle as a torque). No drive: the robot pushes the whole stroke. Casting: solid box, 0.18 kg; friction 0.3 (est).
